label: N-View Computational Methods
notes: This chapter, printed pages 434 through 457, asks how a long set of image measurements becomes a reconstruction. Frame the two pillars: bundle adjustment as the gold-standard nonlinear refinement, and factorization as a direct linear route. Each method is tied to one inspection target, rank, sparsity, conditioning, or connectivity.

label: The Reconstruction Pipeline
notes: Walk the learners through the pipeline shape. Local matching produces tracks and a visibility mask, an initialization route gives a coarse projective structure, and bundle adjustment polishes everything. Stress that every reconstruction stays projective until a metric upgrade or calibration constraint is stated, so ambiguity tracking is part of the workflow.

label: Measurements and the Observation Graph
notes: Define the raw data carefully. Image points indexed by camera and point form a bipartite observation graph whose edges are the visible measurements. Missing data is the rule, not the exception. Bundle adjustment tolerates holes because residuals are local, while direct SVD factorization needs complete tracks, a distinction worth repeating.

label: Bundle Adjustment: The Cost
notes: Introduce the gold standard. Bundle adjustment jointly optimizes all cameras and all points to minimize total squared reprojection error under an assumed noise model. It is maximum likelihood when noise is Gaussian. Emphasize that it needs a good initialization because the cost is non-convex, so it is the last step, not the first.

label: Sparse Structure and Schur Complement
notes: This is the computational heart of the chapter. Each residual touches exactly one camera and one point, so the normal matrix is block-arrowhead sparse. Levenberg-Marquardt with the Schur complement eliminates the large point block first, leaving a small reduced camera system. Walk the partition U, W, V slowly on the diagram.

label: Affine Factorization
notes: Present Tomasi and Kanade. Affine cameras map centroids to centroids, so subtracting each image centroid removes translation and leaves a measurement matrix that factors as motion times structure. The matrix is rank three in the noiseless case, so the closest reconstruction is the rank-three SVD truncation. This is the cleanest result in the chapter.

label: The Factorization W = M S
notes: Make the SVD mechanics concrete. Take the centered two-m by n matrix, compute its SVD, keep the top three singular values, and split the truncated factors into a motion matrix and a structure matrix. The rank-three plateau in the spectrum is the auditable invariant. The remaining linear ambiguity is fixed by metric constraints.

label: Non-Rigid Factorization
notes: Extend the subspace idea to deforming scenes. With l basis shapes each trajectory lives in a 3l-dimensional subspace, so the singular value drop moves from after three to after 3l, here six for two shapes. The motion matrix keeps repeated camera blocks, and the factorization ambiguity is harder, which is the honest caveat to state.

label: Projective Factorization with Depths
notes: Now the projective case. Image points are scale classes, so the equation only becomes a rank-four factorization once the correct projective depths weight each measurement. Unit depths generally do not give rank four. Depths are estimated iteratively, and the row-column scaling freedom is an exact gauge that should be normalized between iterations.

label: Conditioning and Normalization
notes: Drive home the warning that the algebraic matrix is not the geometric error. Isotropic image normalization sharply lowers the effective condition number of the homogeneous system before the SVD, so the same rank-four object is recovered far more reliably. Pair this with the residual descent curve from the bundle solve as a diagnostic habit.

label: Plane-Based and Sequence Methods
notes: Cover two initialization devices. A known reference-plane homography fixes the left three-by-three camera block, leaving a linear homogeneous system for the final columns whose null space is the one-dimensional common scale. For sequences, pairwise and triplet windows are merged into a global start. Both are initializers, not substitutes for final bundle adjustment.

label: Synthesis and Takeaways
notes: Close by tying the routes together. Bundle adjustment is sparse nonlinear least squares on the observation graph; affine factorization is a rank-three approximation; projective factorization needs depths and normalization to mean anything geometric; plane and sequence methods initialize. Always state the remaining projective, affine, or metric ambiguity before claiming success.
